newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Founders Blue Chip.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Founders Blue Chip.

text.p: Brian Kelly gets nervous when he looks at the current picture of rising U.S. consumer debt.

Banks and retailers are handing out credit cards almost with abandon, he believes, and many consumers are grabbing the plastic, with little desire to pay down current debt in these relatively good economic times.
"If consumers are not paying down debt in good economic times, they're not going to do it in difficult times," said Kelly, who took over as portfolio manager of the Founders Blue Chip Fund on July 1.
Fearful of the larger market ramifications, Kelly has steered the fund away from finance companies, such as Money Store Inc, and retailers, such as Gap Inc, Tommy Hilfiger Corp, and Nine West Group.

Kelly believes that stocks in the S&P 500 index and the Dow Industrials are trading at historically low yields. With relief not likely to come from a massive move to raise dividends, stocks are bound for a major correction. The stock market, he said, is in the "danger zone."
In recent weeks, Kelly has assumed a defensive position. He has snapped up big oil stocks, such as Exxon Corp, Mobil Corp, and Williams Cos Inc.
Overall, the fund is slightly overweight on the energy sector, as compared to the S&P 500, with seven percent in oil stocks and five percent in natural gas issues.
Another overweight ranking is the chemical/fertilizer group at five percent. He cited the low U.S. grain inventories as well as expectations for increased demand.
The $474 million fund currently has about 14 percent in U.S. Treasuries, and about six percent in cash.
The top five stock holdings include Bally Entertainment Corp, IES Industries Inc, Arcadian Corp, Williams Cos, and Coca-Cola Co.

Kelly said IES is undervalued, taking into account its stake of about 12 percent in McLeod Inc. The fund held Bally prior to the planned Hilton merger deal, and owned Arcadian shares before the announcement of a planned purchase by Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc.
Kelly said the fund currently has about 110 stocks in the portfolio, and he expects turnover at about 100 percent.
Before Kelly's arrival, year-to-date, the fund has returned 15.99 percent versus 10.03 percent for the average gross and income fund, according to Lipper Analytical Services.
For 1995, the fund returned 29.06 percent versus 30.98 percent for the average fund. Over five years, the annualized return was 13.46 percent versus 13.30 percent for the average fund in the sector.
